en: Gregorio del Pilar was only 24 years old when he heroically died defending the pass at Tirad during the Philippine-American War.
The Philippine Eagle is one of the largest and most powerful eagles in the world, boasting a massive wingspan of up to two meters.
The Commission on Human Rights is an independent constitutional office in the Philippines, meaning it operates completely separately from the three main branches of government.
The Ifugao carved the ancient Banaue Rice Terraces into the mountains using only hand tools, creating staircases that reach up to 1,500 meters above sea level.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct living languages, meaning a Filipino might need to learn a completely new language just by traveling to the next province.
Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a makeshift bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm in rural areas where electricity was completely unavailable.
The MassKara Festival in Bacolod features giant illuminated masks, but it was originally created in 1980 to help locals smile through a severe economic crisis.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence on June 12, 1898, from the window of his ancestral home in Kawit, Cavite, while the national anthem played.
The word bayanihan historically described an entire community physically carrying a traditional nipa hut on bamboo poles to relocate it to a new village.
The rare, golden South Sea Pearl was declared the official national gem of the Philippines in 1996 because of its unique cultivation in local waters.
The Philippine Senate chamber features a unique hemicycle shape so that every single senator can clearly see and hear every other senator during debates.
National Artist Guillermo Tolentino sculpted the massive Bonifacio Monument using concrete and bronze, depicting a torn globe to symbolize the breaking of colonial chains.
